verdict.rationale: Skyfire documents pay/kya-pay tokens that the agent uses in place of a raw card. Each token carries a committed amount that acts as a ceiling, and charges above its remaining balance are rejected. Tokens have a bounded expiry and authorize payment to a seller, and card authorizations cover a specific merchant and amount. However, per-token merchant scoping and expiry configuration are only lightly documented, and in-flight tokens cannot be revoked individually. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of configurable merchant restrictions on pay tokens, detailed expiry-setting controls, a per-token revocation API, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can hand my agent a scoped, limited-use payment credential — amount limits, expiry, merchant restrictions — instead of a raw card number

citations.quote: Charges above the token's remaining balance are rejected.
Tokens may be charged multiple times until their balance is exhausted.
no per-token revocation API is documented, so the practical caps are the token amount and its 10-second-to-24-hour expiry
The agent/agent platform can never spend more than the cardholder approved.
